Hi Jordan,

Attached are our redlines to Redwood's Master Services Agreement (MSA) and DPA. We flagged a few SOW template items as well that we'll want clarified before signing — primarily around data segregation, liability cap, and subcontractor disclosure.

Key asks in summary (see attached PDF):
- Increase liability cap to 3x fees or $5M (we proposed).
- Add explicit audit rights for security assessments.
- Narrow the data processing definition to exclude aggregated telemetry.
- Require notice for third-party subprocessors with 30 days' notice.

Can we set up a 30-minute call next week to walk through these? We're aiming to get an executed agreement by end of June to align with our integration timeline.

Thanks Liam — received and reviewed with legal. I've consolidated Redwood's responses and a clean counter in the attached "Redwood_Counter_MSA_v3.docx" and a one-page redline summary. High-level responses below so you have context before the call: 

1) Liability cap — we can move to a 2x fees or $3M cap for the first year of the relationship, with a performance review tied to customer usage metrics before renewal. This is a compromise from our standard $1.5M cap.

2) Audit rights — we accept a scoped security assessment right (annual, with agreed scoping doc and 30 days' notice) but cannot accept broad, unlimited audit rights that disrupt multi-tenant operations.

3) Data processing — we'll agree to carve out aggregated, anonymized telemetry. We'll add clarifying language for customer data types and retention.

4) Subprocessors — Redwood will continue to provide a subprocessors list and commit to 30 days' notice for new subprocessors; for critical infra changes we'll provide an upgrade path or migration plan.

I've proposed language in the counterdocument that preserves predictable SLOs and protects Redwood's IP for inference optimizations while giving Catalyst the contractual assurances they need.

Proposed next steps:
- Please review the Redwood counter by EOD Friday (Jun 5).
- If acceptable, schedule a 30-minute alignment call next week; Marissa and Marcus can join to handle billing and technical ops questions.

Call times I'm available: Tue 6/8 10:00–11:30am PT, Wed 6/9 1:00–3:00pm PT.

Best,

Jordan Blake

On Tue, Jun 8, 2026 at 09:30 AM Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@catalystanalytics.com> wrote:
> Jordan — appreciate the quick turnaround and the middle-ground on liability. A couple of clarifying questions after reading the counter:
>
> - On the 2x/$3M proposal: does the "first year" clause apply to the initial 12 months post-signature, or to the first contract term? We want it tied to the initial contract term.

Good question — we intended the initial 12-month period post-signature, but we're open to making that explicit and aligning to the "initial contract term" language to avoid ambiguity. I've noted the update for legal to mirror your phrasing.

> - For audit rights: can you share a short scoping template (even a paragraph) that describes permitted audit activities so our auditors can confirm fit?

Yes — see the bullet below which I'll include in the redline: permitted audits are limited to non-disruptive security assessments, performed no more than once per 12 months, with mutually agreed scope, conducted by an accredited third party, and executed with 30 days' advance notice. The vendor (Redwood) will provide remediation timelines for any findings.

> - On subprocessors: will Redwood provide a monthly updated list or only upon change notification? We rely on timely notice for our procurement checks.

We currently provide change-based notifications (30 days). To help Catalyst's procurement process we can provide a monthly exported snapshot URL to the current subprocessors list (read-only link) for the duration of the SOW. We'll add that into the DPA appendix.

Call recap and action items from today's 30-minute alignment call (attendees: Jordan, Olivia, Liam, Marissa, Marcus):
- Redwood to deliver updated counter with: explicit "initial contract term" language, audit scoping paragraph, monthly subprocessors snapshot link (due Jun 10 EOD).
- Catalyst legal to confirm acceptance or provide narrow redlines to the updated counter by Jun 12.
- Commercial note: Marissa to circulate proposed pricing schedule referenced in SOW (separate email).

I'll attach the draft updates once legal has applied changes.

Best,

Jordan Blake
Head of Partnerships
